blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines is looking to the United States as an alternative supplier — and not its sole source of its food and energy requirements as earlier claimed by US President Donald Trump — amid concerns over potential supply disruptions and rising prices, Malacañang said on Sunday. In a video message, Palace press officer Claire Castro said Manila was exploring Washington as one of its potential sources of agricultural and energy products to strengthen the country’s food and energy security, particularly as the Philippines braces for the effects of a very strong El Niño. “The meeting between the leaders […]...
